name: Cuneiform Tablet
desc: A reed stylus impresses wedge-signs into wet clay, sign by sign, down ruled cases: each wedge a triangular depression that catches a raking lamp so that as the light rakes across the tablet the whole relief field shimmers, far rims glinting and near rims falling to shadow. When the tablet fills it dries and a fresh damp slab is set down and the scribe begins again -- a perpetual clerk's desk. Warm ochre clay, fired terracotta, grey diorite stone, or deep lapis picked out in cold light.

energy.doc: impression depth, rim contrast and raking-light glow

scale.doc: wedge / sign size -- larger signs (obvious change)

speed.doc: how fast signs are impressed, the light rakes, and the tablet turns

density.doc: signs per tablet -- tighter case grid

hue.doc: clay tone for the default; other styles fix their own

style.doc: aesthetic: wet ochre clay / fired terracotta / grey diorite stone / lapis in cold luminous light

seed.doc: deterministic -- re-throws the signs, wedge layout and clay toning
